capture.final_message:
Use the evaluation formulas for finite measures viewed as signed measures.

- For the first conjunct, evaluate subtraction pointwise on the measurable set `i`. Rewrite each `μ.toSignedMeasure i` using the characterization as `μ.real i`; subtraction in signed/vector measures is pointwise, so the desired real subtraction follows immediately.

- For the second conjunct, use extensionality for vector measures and test on an arbitrary measurable set `t`. The left side evaluates to `μ.toSignedMeasure (t ∩ s)` (up to the library’s intersection order), while the right side rewrites via `Measure.restrict_apply` and then `Measure.toSignedMeasure_apply` to the same real-valued measure. Resolve any intersection-order mismatch by commutativity.

The finite-measure assumptions are essential because `Measure.toSignedMeasure` uses finite real-valued evaluations; the restricted measure remains finite via `isFiniteMeasureRestrict`.
